title: Recursive Symplectic Weil Character Formula
body_html:
Recursive Symplectic Weil Character Formula

Let \((E,j)\) be a symplectic vector space over a finite field \(k\) of odd order \(q\), and let \(s\in S(E,j)\). Gérardin computes \(\operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E,j}(s)\) by reducing to semisimple elliptic blocks and to smaller symplectic quotients.

If \(s\) acts without fixed point on \(E\setminus\{0\}\), let \(E_+\) be a maximal \(s\)-invariant totally isotropic subspace, and let \(2\ell_0\) be the codimension of \(E_+\) in its orthogonal complement. Then the character is expressed by the Gaussian determinant factor \[ \operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E,j}(s) = \left[ \operatorname{det}_{E_+}(s)\, \operatorname{det}_{E_+^{\mathrm{orth}}/E_+}(s-1)\, (-1)^{\ell_0} \right]^{(1-q)/2}. \]

If \(s\) fixes a line \(E_+\) and there is no \(s\)-invariant supplementary subspace of \(E_+\) in the orthogonal complement of \(E_+\), then \[ \operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E,j}(s) = \operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E_0,j_0}(s_0), \] where \(E_0=E_+^{\mathrm{orth}}/E_+\), and \(j_0,s_0\) are the induced form and induced operator.

If \(s\) fixes a line \(E_+\) and has an \(s\)-invariant supplementary subspace \(E_0\) of \(E_+\) in the orthogonal complement of \(E_+\), then the character is a finite Gaussian sum over the quotient appearing in Gérardin's formula: \[ \operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E,j}(s) = \sum_y \xi\!\left(e^{\,i(sy,y)}\right) \operatorname{Tr} W_\xi^{E_0,j_0}(s_0). \]

The last display records the shape of Gérardin's recursive Gaussian sum. The exact indexing quotient and phase normalization are source-sensitive and should be reviewed before this node is admitted.
